name: Assyrians
place: Ashur and Nineveh on the upper Tigris
desc: Traders first, whose donkey caravans carried tin and cloth into Anatolia, then builders of the largest empire the world had seen, with stone-lined aqueducts, carved palaces guarded by winged bulls, and the great library of Nineveh.
source: The Old Assyrian letters from Kanesh (Kültepe), about 23,000 tablets; Ashurbanipal's library and palace reliefs (British Museum)

gluttonous: led two hundred donkeys loaded with tin across the mountains to Kanesh
belligerent: speared a lion that had broken into the sheepfold
cautious: distilled a scent of myrrh and calamus for the palace

inventions.name: Donkey Caravans
inventions.source: Old Assyrian merchants sent black donkeys with about 65 kg of tin and textiles each the 1,000 km from Ashur to Kanesh
inventions.desc: Strings of pack donkeys with balanced loads: everyone carries 2 more.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication, and long journeys.

inventions.name: Perfume Still
inventions.source: A tablet of about 1200 BCE names Tapputi-Belatekallim, a palace perfumer who distilled flowers, oil and calamus: the first chemist known by name
inventions.desc: Flowers and resins boiled and their vapour caught in a clay lid: +2 mood, and the sick recover 10% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs pottery, and rites at the hearth.

inventions.name: Stone Aqueduct
inventions.source: Sennacherib's aqueduct at Jerwan (c. 690 BCE), built of some two million stones, carried water 80 km to Nineveh
inventions.desc: A stone channel that brings mountain water down to the gardens: farm plots yield 20% more, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and builders who quarry.

inventions.name: Tablet Library
inventions.source: Ashurbanipal (r. 669–631 BCE) gathered over 30,000 tablets at Nineveh, including the Epic of Gilgamesh
inventions.desc: Shelves of tablets, copied from every town and catalogued: the tribe gathers much more lore.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribal Code, and long years of rites and leadership.

foods.name: Mersu Cakes
foods.source: Mersu, a sweet of dates, pistachios and butter, appears in palace and temple records
foods.desc: Dates pounded with nuts and butter into little cakes for feasts: +3 mood.

foods.name: Skewered Locusts
foods.source: A relief from Sennacherib's palace shows servants carrying skewers of locusts to a banquet
foods.desc: Locusts caught in the fields and roasted on sticks: hunger grows 5% slower.
foods.hint: Comes from hunting, and from cooking at the hearth.

finds.name: Pomegranate Trees
finds.desc: Red fruit full of seeds, the sign of plenty in every palace garden.

finds.name: Mosul Alabaster
finds.source: The palace reliefs of Nineveh and Nimrud were carved on slabs of local gypsum alabaster
finds.desc: Soft white stone that takes a fine carving: each load is stone.

people.name: Lamassi
people.source: Wives of Kanesh merchants ran the looms at Ashur and wrote to their husbands about cloth, prices and debts
people.desc: She weaves the cloth the caravans carry, and writes sharp letters to whoever owes her.
memory: wove twelve fine cloths in one winter for the caravan

people.name: Ennam-Ashur
people.desc: He knows every pass to Kanesh and every toll along the way.
memory: brought the caravan home through a snowstorm with every donkey alive

people.name: Tapputi-Belatekallim
people.desc: Overseer of the palace perfumers, who distilled and filtered her scents: the first chemist whose name survives.

people.name: Ashurbanipal
people.source: His own inscriptions; the library of Nineveh, excavated from 1849
people.desc: A king who boasted he could read stones from before the Flood, and sent scribes across the empire to copy every tablet they found.

people.name: Pushu-ken
people.source: One of the best-documented merchants of the Kanesh archives, c. 1900 BCE
people.text: a merchant with a string of black donkeys and a bundle of letters from his wife.
memory: paid the toll at every town between Ashur and Kanesh, and argued at every one
people.desc: An Assyrian trader in Anatolia whose business letters, with his wife Lamassi back home, survive by the dozen.

people.name: Sammu-ramat
people.label: Sammu-ramat the Queen Regent
people.desc: A queen who ruled for her son and became the legend of Semiramis. Lore 6, Combat 5.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.label: Sennacherib the Water-Bringer
people.desc: He brings mountain water to a garden city. Crafting 8.

people.name: Tiglath-Pileser
people.label: Tiglath-Pileser the Conqueror
people.desc: A king who makes the army a standing force. Combat 8, 85 HP.

events.title: Lions at the Sheepfold
events.source: Assyrian kings hunted lions as a royal duty: the lion hunt reliefs of Ashurbanipal
events.text: A great beast has been taking sheep at night. The young hunters beg to go after it; the elders want a higher wall.

options.label: Hunt it down

do.alert: The beast is out there. Gather the spears!

options.result: The hunters go out with torches. The beast is waiting.

options.label: Raise the fold walls
options.result: Thorns and stones go up around the fold. The losses stop.

events.title: Ten Days of Feasting
events.source: The Banquet Stele of Ashurnasirpal II (879 BCE) records 69,574 guests fed for ten days at the opening of Kalhu
events.text: The new village is finished. The chief wants a feast that will be remembered in every camp around: ten days of bread, beer and meat for anyone who comes.

options.label: Hold the feast

do.feat: Held a feast of ten days

options.result: They come from every valley. For years afterwards strangers greet our people by the name of that feast.

options.label: A modest meal
options.result: The people eat together quietly and go back to work.

events.title: The Locusts Come
events.source: Letters to Assyrian kings report locust swarms and the efforts to destroy their eggs
events.text: A brown cloud comes over the hills and settles on the fields. By evening the barley is stubble. The children, at least, have discovered that locusts roasted on a stick are good to eat.

tales.name: Etana Rides the Eagle
tales.source: The Myth of Etana; copies from Ashurbanipal's library
tales.text: King Etana had no son. He rescued an eagle from a pit where a snake had thrown it, and the eagle carried him up toward heaven to find the plant of birth. Higher they flew, until the land was a garden plot and the sea a water trough, and Etana grew afraid.
tales.moral: kindness repaid can lift you high

tales.name: Ishtar Goes Down to the Underworld
tales.source: The Descent of Ishtar, Neo-Assyrian version
tales.text: Ishtar went down to the land of no return. At each of the seven gates she gave up a jewel or a garment, until she stood bare before her sister, queen of the dead. While she lay below, no bull mounted a cow and no seed sprouted on the earth, until the gods sent for her.

tales.name: The Seven Sages from the Sea
tales.source: Apkallu sages, carved on the palace reliefs of Nimrud; Berossus
tales.text: Before the Flood, seven sages came up out of the sea, wearing cloaks of fish skin. They taught people to build cities and temples, to write, to measure fields and to make laws. Then they went back into the water, and the carvers still put them at the palace doors to keep out evil.
tales.moral: wisdom is a gift to be passed on

tales.name: Ashurbanipal's Boast
tales.text: I learned the art of the sage, says the king. I can solve problems of division and multiplication that have no answer. I have read the artful script of Sumer and the obscure Akkadian, and I have read stones from before the Flood. Then he went lion hunting.
